comments.value: This could mean the death of the platform if not addressed
Nobody likes clicking on something and finding out that the actual content looks nothing like what was advertised.

Honestly, there really ought to be a tagging system as soon as possible, no matter how good the AI ​​looks, it is important to disclose that the created world contains AI-generated content with which users will interact
As a creator of worlds and avatars, if something isnt done about this i will reconsider the financial support i give VRC

Been seeing another GPT-6 Astra made world do its rounds. I have already seen people make posts about it not knowing it was created with AI. Still silence from VRChat. A few creators have already started to leave the platform. The longer VRChat does nothing the worse this problem will become.

To add insult to injury VRChat has decided to promote at least one AI generated world in a curated worlds spotlight today. I suspect that there are others made with AI that we don't know about because there is NO TAG FOR AI CONTENT.
I support this. I'd also like an option to completely hide worlds, avatars and such made with ai, not just label them as such.
Asset ripping and reverse-engineering are against VRChat's TOS, tools that only exist because they ripped and reverse-engineered our work easily constitute a breach of TOS.

I think this would also be a nice thing to have to filter out people mass producing slop - blocking a user should hide their worlds for you

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/blocking-user-should-hide-their-worlds
The minimum I would like to see is a content tag on upload.
@{62df1f0a67455d44a15a629a|full_name} New update, VRChat has completely blocked comments on their Steam posts.

@{5cb0e62414ddd360bbe1ac29|full_name} Not new, they've been like that for a while. They had a few posts earlier this year where they seemingly forgot to lock the thread and the comments are an interesting glimpse into how the greater community perceives the game. But turning off comments in the first place just goes to show how VRC really feels about its community. See no evil...

details:
Just today I have seen 3 X/Twitter posts of fully AI generated worlds made using GPT-6 Astra, one of them already published.

https://x.com/yuipxq/status/2097025460295389601

https://x.com/kurotori4423/status/2097011323767034098

https://x.com/pichikyo/status/2096285284178788612

I fear this kind of content will soon flood the platform. VRChat needed to add some kind of AI tag or descriptor a long time ago. This kind of quickly and effortlessly generated content hurts existing creators on this platform.

Please don't let this become another "too little, too late" situation. VRChat needs an identifier for AI generated content added ASAP. Regardless of how end users personally feel about the use of AI, a way to separate and identify AI generated content from user created content is an absolute necessity.
title: Add an AI content identifier for worlds and avatars
